Substitui o plan mode interativo; usada isoladamente ou como etapa 1 do /implement.

{"body":"Part of #35 (section 3, enhancement 8 — the human half). Depends on #45 (the tile-grid runtime) and #44 (scene layers, as the placement target).

## The gap

#45 gives the engine a grid that turns painted cells into an autotiled, collided, streamed world — but "painted" so far means *programmatically*. This is the human half: open the editor, pick "Dirt" from the shelf, and **drag**.

## Three pieces of craft that separate "works" from "feels right"

**1. Strokes are drag-interpolated.** A fast mouse gives scattered samples 20–60px apart, not a line; naive painting turns a confident swipe into a dotted trail of orphan cells. The paint system interpolates between samples, the way every art program has worked since MacPaint. The difference between "this tool feels right" and "this tool fights me" is exactly this line of maths.

**2. One stroke = one undo step.** Paint a 200-cell ridge, change your mind — that must be ONE Ctrl+Z, not 200. `TileGridPaintCommand` accumulates the gesture and commits it as a unit. Without this, undo is technically present and practically useless.

**3. You paint meaning and you SEE meaning.** While painting, `TileGridOverlay` draws each cell in its value's flat colour (Dirt brown, Water blue, Eraser clearing) — the logical grid, unambiguous. The baked art reskins underneath; toggling flips between "what I said" and "what it looks like".

Around those: the `GroundPaint` tool mode (promoted from a reserved comment in `GizmoStateComponent`, + `PaintValue` selection), the palette shelf swapping to **value cards** when an indexed layer is active (plus a `+ New` index card), and the defaults that made painting pleasant — snap on, grid visible, drag paints tile-per-cell.

## Delivery

- [ ] Port `System/TileGridPaintSystem.cs` (198 lines), `Tile/TileGridOverlay.cs` (205), `Undo/TileGridPaintCommand.cs`
- [ ] Wiring: `GizmoStateComponent` (`EditorToolMode.GroundPaint`, `PaintValue`), `PalettePlacementSystem` (value cards, `ArmPaint*`), `EditorOverlayPrepSystem`, `EditorOverlay` composition
- [ ] Premises entry: Paint tab; drag-interpolated strokes are ONE undo step
- [ ] Test: an interpolated stroke leaves no gaps at any drag speed; one stroke undoes/redoes as a unit; eraser round-trips; painting a locked layer refuses loudly

Reference implementation: `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/level-editor/…`

**Value on its own:** with #45 alone, MonoDreams has an LDtk-grade runtime usable only from code. With this, *person opens editor, paints a playable level, saves `.mdscene`* is real — the single biggest usability jump the editor can make.
